findings.title: On the next SIM_VERSION bump the rematch golden is re-blessed with no proof that covers a rematch
findings.claim: duel-rematch.json is now a pinned artifact, but a bump is allowed by only two proofs: the sector version-only comparison and the duel oracle. Neither one ever runs a rematch, the end card or a second round. So at SIM 39→40, `npm run bless` would rewrite duel-rematch.json even if startRound, stepDecided, followingSeed or the tick-stamp shift had changed. The comment in bless-golden.ts says the golden is re-blessed 'on the same proofs as duel-1.json', but those proofs never touch the run it pins.
findings.evidence: scripts/bless-golden.ts:L2-4 (the comment: 'the oracle's runs never rematch, so a bump re-blesses it on the same proofs as duel-1.json'); bless-golden.ts:L27-29 (the rematch golden joins storedVersions and names); scripts/golden/blessGuard.ts:L26-35 (a bump runs only verify() and duel()); scripts/golden/duelOracle.ts:L43-46 (ORACLE_RUNS are the scripted and passive gate seeds 1-10 only) and L195 (each run stops at its outcome, so no oracle run reaches the end card); duelOracle.ts:L91 (MIGRATIONS[38]: 'no oracle run sends rematch'); tests/helpers/scriptedDuel.ts:L93-113 (runRematch: the only rematch run, used only by bless and the golden test). Indirect cover: the suite's round-start equivalence test (tests/duelRounds.test.ts:L104-128) checks only 600 ticks of round 2. It is not part of the bless guard, and it never checks the end-card ticks or the rematch tick.
findings.why: Brief item 8 and the severity list count 'a golden can be re-blessed without proof' as a blocking class. The guard's own rule is that a pinned duel artifact is never re-blessed on a bump unless every run matches per tick (blessGuard.ts:L6-8). That rule does not hold for duel-rematch.json. Its whole job is to pin round-2 behaviour, and a bump that silently changes round 2 would pass. I rate this P1 rather than P0 because the spec's §7 sequence (spec L288-292) set it up this way, and part of the trace is covered indirectly: the oracle's seed-2 run plus the equivalence test.
findings.fix: Add a rematch run to ORACLE_RUNS, for example `{ id: 'rematch-1', seed: 1, crew: 'scripted', rematch: true }`. recordRun would step through the end card, send player 0's rematch on the first end-card tick and run round 2 to its outcome, as runRematch does, keeping the per-tick digests of results, events and telemetry. Record it in the SIM 39 baseline, so the next bump proves the rematch path per tick. Also tie the baseline to the stored rematch golden, as goldenRefusal does for duel-1.json. Until then, correct the bless-golden.ts comment. Alternatively, make blessRefusal refuse a bump when the rematch golden is stale unless a rematch-aware proof passes.

findings.title: runRematch does not check that the scripted commands were applied, unlike runDuel
findings.claim: runDuel throws when any scripted command is not applied, so the duel golden can never pin a run in which the script is being rejected. runRematch drops the results of both rounds' scripted steps. Round 2 runs with every tick offset by baseTick, so a stale-tick or not-at-weapons rejection there would be blessed into the golden without any error.
findings.evidence: tests/helpers/scriptedDuel.ts:L44-50 (runDuel's applied-status check) against L99-100 (runRematch: `stepDuelTick(d, input); recordTick(t, d, input)` with the results discarded).
findings.why: Round 2 is the only part of the rematch golden that no other pinned artifact covers. A silently rejected script would make it pin degenerate behaviour.
findings.fix: In play(), keep stepDuelTick's results and throw on any status other than 'applied', with the same message runDuel gives, before recordTick.

verified: Decision 2 (plan L50): roundModule has the fields round, helmPlayer, baseTick and decidedTick, with id 'round', and sits after repair and before interior in DUEL_MODULES (src/renderer/src/sim/duel/modules.ts:L812-826, L82). flattenDuel's order is tested at tests/duelModules.test.ts L2008.

Decision 3 (plan L51): stepDecided calls startRound(d, tick + 1), so baseTick is T+1 (step.ts L1282 in the diff). duelRules.step replaces the accumulator on a round change and does not record the rematch tick, so ticks starts at 0 (duelRules.ts L437 in the diff). The checkpoint test at the rematch passes because ticks = tick − base = 0.

Decision 4 (plan L52): a fresh tactical state has graceUntil all 0, fireAt −1 and lastLaunch −HUNTER_MISSILE_COOLDOWN_TICKS (src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/state.ts:L106,L130). startRound fills graceUntil with T and adds T to lastLaunch (step.ts L1251-1252). fireAt is −1 at a fresh start, so leaving it alone is correct. The tactical sources have no other tick stamps (grep on sim/tactical: only hunter.ts:91-96, duel.ts:29 and contacts.ts:17-39). The equivalence test shifts exactly these stamps (duelRounds.test.ts L113,L119).

Decision 5 (plan L53): startRound runs createDuel before disposeDuel(d), then Object.assign(d, next), so a fresh interior world is used and the DuelState identity is kept (step.ts L1246-1255). The tests assert a new interior object and save/load hash equality for 600 ticks after a rematch (duelRounds.test.ts L95, L129-143).

Decision 6 (plan L54): stepDecided checks a rematch for stale-tick, then unavailable (player absent at the tick's start, from presentBefore), then noop for a second one. Presence is applied, every other duel kind is rejected duel-decided, any other kind gets not-in-duel, and tactical and repair events are cleared (step.ts L1260-1285). In the running step a rematch is rejected duel-running (L1321). Both are tested at duelRounds.test.ts L58-84 and L147-178.

Decision 7 (plan L55): core.ts:L446 calls records(previousCues, state) after the cues and before previousCues is updated. The cue baseline is { outcome, round }. records emits exactly once, on the tick where the round is unchanged and the outcome leaves Running. The victory/defeat cue is guarded the same way, so the rematch tick and end-card ticks emit no cue or record. The duel never ends (terminal: ended false). Tested at duelRounds.test.ts L179-194.

Decision 8 and the widened summary: duelEndSummary carries every Helm §13 field, missileLosses is in MISSILE_LOSSES order, and the codec's duelSummaryShape matches it field for field (summary.ts L1377-1395; codec.ts L613-622). The round event is admitted only by the duel codec (codecModeWire.test.ts L1601-1611).
Decision 9 (plan L57): the layout cache is keyed by the layout object, bounded at 4, and validation still compares layoutId and layoutHash (snapshot.ts L989-994, L1032-1033).

Decision 10 (plan L58): roundSeed refuses a round above MAX_DUEL_ROUNDS before any chain work, and keeps the chain for up to 4 init seeds. The snapshot refuses round > 1024 and 2·round > baseTick before the checkpoint validator calls roundSeed (seeds.ts L891-900; snapshot.ts L1076-1079; duelCheckpoint.ts L367-368). The worst case for a forged checkpoint is bounded at about 1024×16 map generations.

The round module cannot be forged past validation: round is an integer in 0..1024, helm is 0/1, base is in 0..tick with 2·round ≤ base, and decided is −1 exactly while the outcome is Running, otherwise in base..tick. The hash is checked over all values. The checkpoint ties seed = roundSeed(init.seed, round), helmPlayer = init.helmPlayer, telemetry ticks = (decided ? decidedTick : tick) − baseTick, and the outcome agreement (snapshot.ts L1074-1080; duelCheckpoint.ts L367-383). Tests: duelSnapshot.test.ts L116-143 and duelRounds.test.ts L222-226.

The caches cannot return a stale validity. Seed entries are pure functions of the seed, and the private shape is read only by validateTacticalValues. A test shows hashTactical of the shape is unchanged after 10,000 validations, and that accept/reject is identical whether the entry is cached or evicted (duelCache.test.ts L37-66).

restoreDuelSnapshot checks digest, version, layout and seed, then runs the same writeBack as loadDuelSnapshot (unflatten, tick agreement, hashDuel equal to the header) and clears per-tick events. This matches the sector's in-place restoreSnapshot pattern (src/renderer/src/sim/snapshot.ts:L72-77). A new round always has a new seed (followingSeed ≥ seed+1), so a cross-round restore is refused (snapshot.ts L1122-1128).

Round 1 is unchanged. In the running step the only changes are the duel-running rejection, which no oracle run sends, and the new decidedTick write. recordTick with baseTick 0 matches the old guard, and the old 'tick < t.ticks' early return after the end still matches the new outcome guard. MIGRATIONS[38] adds only /^round\.(round|helmPlayer|baseTick|decidedTick)$/ (duelOracle.ts L137). The oracle also digests results, events and telemetry per tick (duelOracle.ts L212).

The accumulator freezes: recordTick returns once t.outcome is no longer Running, and the session's summary is computed once. The end-card capture restores exactly the emitted record (telemetry.ts:L93; duelRules.ts L437-439; duelRounds.test.ts L195-208).
Single player (H-1) is unaffected. app/duel/runtime.ts stops stepping once the outcome leaves Running (runtime.ts:L217, L258) and calls createDuel with the default helmPlayer 0 (L196, L268).
Sector paths are unaffected. sectorWire.events returns [] (codec.ts L610). records is optional and the sector does not define it. The sector's schemaVersion stays 1 (src/network/modes/sector.ts:L19).

Boundaries hold. seeds.ts imports only ./snapshot, and step.ts imports ./seeds and ./state; there are no imports from authority/, clientControl/, app/ or render/, and no import cycle (snapshot.ts does not import seeds or step).

The bless guard for the current change: the rematch golden was created with --fresh at 39, when every other artifact was already at 39, so the guard took the same-version path. blessGuard.test.ts pins the new names list (L1538).
